authors: Frank J. Millero, Leslie M. Connaughton, Faina Vinokurova, Peter V. Chetirkin
title: PVT Properties of Concentrated Aqueous Electrolytes. III. Volume Changes for Mixing the Major Sea Salts at I = 1.0 and 3.0 at 25 C
experimental_method: Densities of binary and mixed solutions of NaCl, Na2SO4, MgSO4, MgCl2 at constant molal ionic strength (1.0 and 3.0) at 25 C measured with a Picker vibrating flow densimeter and a Mettler/Paar vibrating densimeter as differences from pure water.
uncertainties_stated: Temperature controlled to +-0.005 C (set to +-0.002 C); estimated densities agree with the measured values within +-30 ppm (I = 1.0) and +-125 ppm (I = 3.0), a statement about the model comparison, not a stated measurement uncertainty.
quality_remarks: Only one of the duplicate or triplicate measured sets is printed for each mixture (footnote a). Ionic strengths of the actual end-point stock solutions deviate from the nominal value (I(2), I(3), Mean I printed under each block; worst: MgSO4-MgCl2 I(3) = 0.98976, MgCl2-Na2SO4 I(2) = 0.99009). Odd value kept as printed: MgCl2 (2)-Na2SO4 (3), I = 1.0, y3 = 0 has 10^3 Delta d = 35.342, while the next row (y3 = 0.09642) is 26.744 and the pure MgCl2 end points of the other MgCl2 series at I = 1.0 are 25.582 (MgCl2-NaCl); the 35.342 is probably a misprint for 25.342 but this is a guess, not a correction. Molalities of the stock solutions come from the 25 C density equations of state. The pure-salt end points of the same binary at the same I differ slightly between series (e.g. NaCl at I = 1.0: 39.170, 39.185, 39.194), reflecting stock-solution differences.
